page: Microsoft Azure M48ls_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the MSMediumMemoryv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on dedicated x86_64 Intel processing architecture, supplying 48 dedicated vCPUs alongside 768.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a high memory allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, designed explicitly to sustain memory-heavy workloads requiring wide operational address spaces without physical hardware oversubscription.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, designated as None for local storage capacity. It is capable of Premium Storage connectivity to external Azure managed disks for persistence and high IOPS workloads. Network operations are decoupled from bundled public IPv4 routing, including zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses upon deployment. The platform operates purely on centralized compute and memory resources without hardware GPU accelerators.

Relative to its hardware classification, the M48ls_v4 delivers strong resource density for enterprise tasks constrained primarily by memory bounds rather than extreme compute parallelism or local NVMe scratch space. The trade-off centers on reliance on network-attached storage architectures and the absence of onboard ephemeral storage, which requires provisioning external disk resources. The server is well aligned for large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, substantial data caching layers, and high-throughput analytics pipelines.

The instance contains no integrated local storage, requiring attached Premium Storage managed disks for storage needs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. It is suited for large enterprise relational databases, in-memory key-value caches, enterprise applications, and substantial data analytics workloads.
